decision.question: Does chalk-like mark-making render both giraffes and the substantial surrounding scene?
decision.criteria: Pass if chalk-like contours, powdery or broken strokes, layered strokes, or rubbed chalk shading visibly describe both giraffes and substantial surrounding regions. These are alternative manifestations of chalk, not features that must all occur everywhere. Broad rubbed shading can qualify when its direction, boundaries, layering or pigment variation describes depicted forms; uniform grain or loss of sharpness alone cannot. Inspect the giraffes separately from the vegetation, hills, sky and ground: convincing marks in one region cannot substitute for chalk rendering in the other. Fail if either the giraffes or substantial surrounding regions are rendered only by photographic detail, generic grain, blur or smearing without form-describing chalk marks. Color, smooth blended passages, recognizable anatomy and retained composition are permitted. Return unknown only if visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
